versions.statuteQuote: Maintain in good and safe working order and condition all electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, air-conditioning, and other facilities and appliances, including elevators, supplied or required to be supplied by him

summaryForModel: The landlord must keep the electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning systems and supplied appliances in good and safe working order. A lease that shifts repair of these major systems to the tenant conflicts with this, unless it is a good-faith written agreement for specified repairs under § 55.1-1220(D).
paraphraseExamples: Tenant is responsible for all repairs to the HVAC system, water heater, and plumbing.
Resident shall maintain and repair all appliances at Resident's expense.
Tenant accepts the premises as-is and is responsible for all maintenance.
tenantExplanation: Virginia makes your landlord keep heating, cooling, plumbing, electrical, and supplied appliances working. A lease generally can't hand those repairs to you.
action: You can ask your landlord to change this so major system and appliance repairs stay with them, unless you caused the damage.
